summary: Chih-mien Adrian Tseng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under James A. Benn, Nobuyoshi Yamabe, and Canshan Cheng, and was attested as assistant professor at Fo Guang University in 2016.

Chijo Akamatsu (1886–1960) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo under Bunzaburo Matsumoto. He held professorships at Keijo Imperial University (1927–1941), Ryukoku University, Koyasan University, Hanazono University, and Yamaguchi University.
Chijun Hamada works in Buddhist studies. In 1978, he held posts at Taisho University as an assistant and as a researcher at its Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute.

Chikafumi Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a master's degree at the University of British Columbia under Karin Preisendanz and Ashok Aklujkar, and earned a PhD from the University of Calgary supervised by Leslie S. Kawamura.

Chiken Kato (1943–2017) was a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University around 1962–1972 and served as a professor at Tokyo Polytechnic University as attested in 2006.
Chiko Corona is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued traditional studies under Kenko Yamashita and Shohaku Okumura.

Chikyo Yamamoto (1910–1988) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served on the faculty of Koyasan University as a professor, attested in 1970, and later as a part-time lecturer, attested in 1980.

Chime Rinpoche (1941–2026) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied traditionally under Khenpo Gangshar around 1957–1959. He held an appointment at the British Library from around 1965 to 1985.

Chin Kung (1927–2022) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Dongmei Fang, Lee Ping-nan, and the 7th Changkya Khutukhtu. He headed the Pure Land Learning College and taught at Chinese Culture University.

Ching Keng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Around 2009, he served as an associate professor at National Chengchi University.

Ching-mei Shyu specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi under Jan Nattier and received her PhD from Cornell University in 2008 under Daniel Boucher and Hubert Durt.
Chirapat Prapandvidya (born 1941) is an Indologist. He founded Silpakorn University, where he also served as director and taught Kazuhiro Yamamoto.

Chisan Kohō (1879–1967) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and Kyōdō Kōshūin. He founded Tsurumi University in 1966 and held leadership roles at Saijō-ji, Nagano Ken Senmon Nisodo, and Soji-ji.

Chishō Namai (born 1945) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has spent his career at Koyasan University, where he served as a professor, attested in 1996, and later as president, attested in 2008.

Chitai Takenaka (born 1945) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University from around 1964 to 1968. He served as an assistant professor at Hanazono University and later as a professor at Tokoha Gakuen University.
Chiyong Kim is a Buddhist studies scholar who held professorships at International Buddhist University and Shitennoji Junior College, both attested in 1976.

Chizen Akanuma (1884–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, Kōkōdō, and under Manshi Kiyozawa and Vagirajnana Jnanissara. He co-founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921 and was a professor at Otani University.

Chizuko Yoshimizu (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed a doctorate at the University of Vienna. She has held posts at the Naritasan Institute, the University of Lausanne, and the University of Tsukuba.

Chlodwig H. Werba specializes in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Vienna, where he served as a professor as attested between 1997 and 2006, and remained affiliated in 2022.
Chogye Shabdrung (born 1981) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College in 2003 and was a student of Sonam Gyatso.
